patients.label: Index patient, 4-year-1-month-old girl

identity_evidence.quote: We present a case of a 4-year-old female

attribution_limitations: The article states the patient was diagnosed with IgA vasculitis while also describing the diagnosis as inconclusive; no biopsy of skin or bowel with IgA deposition is reported.

Systemic lupus erythematosus and inflammatory bowel disease were considered; lab results did not support lupus and the normal fecal calprotectin made IBD less likely, but no ANA, anti-dsDNA or other lupus results are reported.

Perioperative corticosteroid exposure is described only in the Discussion; the case narrative does not name the drug, dose or route, and the authors speculate about its effects on the rash and symptoms.

The first discharge is described as the next day, while a CRP of 7.4 mg/L is labeled at discharge after corticosteroid treatment; the table row does not state which discharge applies beyond that wording.
